indicators.note: the word first tells us the hindrance comes ahead of the single letter a

parts.note: an impediment is an obstacle or hindrance

explanation.surface: Luggage gets in the way before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causes' is just a link; 'first' puts the synonym for hindrance before A even though A is printed earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Impedimenta is a formal, Latin-derived word for encumbering luggage or equipment, especially an army's.

indicators.note: containing means the rug word holds the hole word inside it

parts.note: a mat is a small rug
O, a round letter, looks like a hole

explanation.surface: Throw away a rug that has a hole in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A moat is a water-filled trench or ditch around a castle.

clue.text: Fear pal could have something on his cap

explanation.surface: A friend afraid of something perched on his hat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear flap is a fold of material on a hat that can be turned down to warm the ears.

parts.note: read not as a dairy spread but as a creature of the peaks that butts with its horns

explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild goat of the Alps and other high ranges, and goats are famous for butting.

parts.note: suggests social acceptance, but literally means someone stopped being outside by going in

explanation.definitionFit: To have gone in is to have stopped standing outside, so it is the past tense of going inside.

clue.text: Difficult journey from amphitheatre Ken made

explanation.surface: Ken built a gruelling route from an ancient arena.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long, arduous journey, usually on foot.

clue.text: What Inuits do to fish will improve the party

explanation.surface: Arctic fishermen and party hosts share a technique.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, people fishing on frozen water cut through it; figuratively the idiom means easing initial tension among strangers.

clue.text: Not the friend to have during a crisis or rain?

definitions.text: Not the friend to have during a crisis or rain?

parts.words: Not the friend to have during a crisis or rain?
parts.note: a companion who stays only in good times, read literally as one present only in sunny conditions

explanation.definitionFit: A fair-weather friend is loyal only when things go well, deserting you in hard times.

parts.note: could describe a cautious bonfire, but means using less petrol or other combustible matter

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes how efficiently a vehicle uses petrol, so good efficiency means less is consumed.

clue.text: Soldiers suspect sailor, the Parisian to be feared

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to doubt is to suspect
AB is an able seaman
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Troops distrust a seaman and a Frenchman, who seem formidable.
explanation.definitionFit: Redoubtable means formidable, worthy of fear or respect.

parts.note: a word spoken by conjurors as though uttering it performs magic

explanation.definitionFit: It is a conjuror's magic word, uttered to make a trick happen.

clue.text: Big defeat not completing the course

indicators.note: not completing means the word for course loses its final letter

parts.note: a route is a course or way

explanation.surface: A heavy loss for the runner who failed to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a decisive defeat in which the losers flee in disorder.

parts.note: sounds like rising out of poverty but describes the raised edge beside a road drain

explanation.walkthrough: KERB is the British spelling of curb, the raised stone edge of a pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: The stone edge of the pavement rises a step above the roadside drainage channel.

explanation.surface: A herb offered as a cure for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Valerian is a plant traditionally called by this name, and the name literally promises to cure every ailment.

clue.text: Deal out about a litre of soup with this?

definitions.text: Deal out about a litre of soup with this?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the litre abbreviation
out signals the letters of deal are put out of order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: Serving soup by the litre with a kitchen utensil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DEAL to LADE, and 'about' puts L inside it; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladle is a deep long-handled spoon for serving soup.

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

indicators.note: converted means the letters of gaol are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A sheltered path beside a prison that has been redeveloped.
explanation.walkthrough: GAOL is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A pergola is an arbour or covered walkway with climbing plants on a framework.

indicators.note: over signals the letters of I wept are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher weeping over a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pewit, or peewit, is the lapwing, a plover named for its call.

clue.text: It's like a book that's being called for

explanation.surface: A volume that someone has asked for.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with numbered leaves resembles a volume; someone summoned over a tannoy has been sent for.

parts.note: a checkmark showing correctness, joked about as the sound that marks time on a clock

explanation.definitionFit: A check mark shows something is right, and a clock makes this sound each second.

clue.text: Swedish group sees Bardot enter the AA

parts.note: AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
BB is Brigitte Bardot, French film star known by her initials

explanation.definitionFit: Abba were the Swedish pop quartet who won Eurovision in 1974.

clue.text: Natural ability of leading lady in the exhibition

parts.note: a fair is a trade show or exhibition

indicators.note: leading means the first letter of lady is used

explanation.surface: The leading lady showed real talent at the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is an instinctive talent or aptitude.

parts.note: flat means level or even
let means leased or rented out

explanation.surface: A tiny apartment that has been rented out on fair terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatlet is a very small self-contained flat, typically one room.

indicators.note: in means the egg letter is placed inside the word for roll

O resembles an egg in shape

explanation.surface: Perhaps a chicken, with an egg in a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks the definition as an example: a cock is a male chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is a male domestic fowl, so it is one kind of chicken.

indicators.note: almost means the word for distinguished loses its last letter

parts.note: ennobled means dignified or distinguished

explanation.surface: Nearly honoured, a commoner is raised to the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to the nobility, giving them a title such as baron, is to create a peer.

clue.text: Musical composition number two, say, before two hundred at a finish

say signals that the number is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: two is a number, whose sound gives the spelling heard
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two of them is CC

explanation.surface: A piece of music is the second item, ahead of two hundred at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finish' is a link word indicating the pieces end the assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard piece, often fast and showy.

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
p is piano, the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: Beside a river flowing softly lies a campsite.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp is a place where tents are pitched.

clue.text: Fairy needing scope to see over the top

parts.note: a periscope lets you look over a parapet or above water
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fairy needs a telescope to see over the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is read as wanting in the sense of lacking: a periscope without SCOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy or sprite of Persian mythology.

clue.text: Jug we brought up with royal monogram

parts.note: ER is the cipher of Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: We carried a jug bearing the Queen's insignia upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed pitcher.

clue.text: A songbird for the most part having wings

indicators.note: for the most part means the songbird word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lark is a singing bird

explanation.surface: A songbird mostly takes to the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Alar is a technical adjective meaning relating to wings, from Latin ala.

indicators.note: included means the model letter goes inside the Scots word for one

parts.note: ane is the Scots form of one
Model T was the famous Ford car

explanation.surface: A Scottish fashion model joined the line-up beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Ante is a Latin prefix meaning before, as in antenatal.

clue.text: Gold weight found in the park

parts.note: gold is a yellow colour
a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Panning for gold, a heavy nugget turns up in a park.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellowstone is the famous US national park in Wyoming.

parts.note: winter is one of the seasons
green is a colour

explanation.surface: A shrub that shows its colour in the cold months.
